newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ING,Nomura in Czech IPB tender.
newsitem.headline: ING,Nomura in Czech IPB tender.

text.p: Officials at a Czech government privatisation agency said on Wednesday Dutch ING Bank and Japan's Nomura were the last two bidders remaining in a government tender to buy 36 percent in bank IPB a.s..

National Property Fund (NPF) spokesman Milos Ruzicka confirmed an earlier statement on the issue by the fund's Second Vice-chairman, Michal Hruby, who is the NPF's representative on the bank's supervisory board.
Hruby was not immediately available for comment.

IPB, the country's third largest bank, has become embroiled in one of the country's biggest business scandals after the police on Tuesday took its two highest ranking management members into custody for alleged fraud.

But Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said earlier on Wednesday the government was committed to the selloff despite the investigation which has brought charges against IPB's Director Jiri Tesar and Deputy Director Libor Prochazka.
The CTK news agency reported that a court decided on Wednesday the suspects would be held in custody until trial to prevent them from influencing witnesses.
ING and Nomura have been widely tipped as the leading participants in the tender, and NPF chairman Roman Ceska has said Nomura had the "best chance" of winning the tender.
However, the sale must be approved by the whole cabinet where Ceska does not have a seat.
Ruzicka also confirmed that Hruby said the head of Nomura's Czech representative office, Eduard Onderka, is also the representative of Nutshell s.r.o. which holds a 9.8 percent stake in the bank.
